characterized_levers.name: Technical Feasibility Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Demonstrating technical feasibility impacts policy. Immediate: Demonstrators built → Systemic: 15% increased policy traction due to concrete evidence → Strategic: Enhanced credibility in procurement negotiations.
options: Focus demonstrator efforts on a single, highly secure authentication method, such as FIDO2, on a mainstream Android device.
Develop demonstrators for both FIDO2 on GrapheneOS and a browser-based fallback, accepting slightly longer development timelines.
Explore passwordless authentication via blockchain-anchored identity and decentralized identifiers (DIDs) alongside FIDO2 and browser-based fallback demonstrators.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Technical Risk vs. Scope. Weakness: The options don't explicitly address the cost implications of each demonstrator approach.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on demonstrating technical feasibility to impact policy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of the technical demonstrators on policy traction, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to demonstrator development.
characterized_levers.description: Technical Feasibility Strategy validates platform-neutral and fallback authentication concepts through non-production demonstrators, delivering concrete technical evidence to inform policy and procurement. It scopes and manages technical risk, selects demonstrator approaches (e.g., FIDO2 on GrapheneOS and a browser-based fallback), and defines success metrics such as demonstrator completeness, security posture, interoperability with OpenID Connect, and documented cost and schedule implications. It interfaces with Policy Advocacy Strategy, Coalition Building Strategy, and Procurement Influence Strategy by providing credible prototypes and risk assessments that reduce uncertainty and accelerate informed decision-making during phase transitions, while balancing security, privacy, and feasibility within budget constraints.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Strong synergies with Policy Advocacy Strategy and Coalition Building Strategy. Demonstrator results translate technical feasibility into policy proposals and coalition messaging, providing credible evidence of platform-neutral viability. This evidence also underpins procurement discussions by offering concrete risk assessments, timelines, and interoperability guarantees that coalition partners can rally around.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Trade-offs may constrain Procurement Influence Strategy and EU Standards Engagement Strategy. Resource-intensive demonstrations could slow procurement language development or EU-standard alignment, risking misalignment with budget and governance timelines. If procurement priorities demand immediate language or EU consensus, the technical exploration could be deprioritized, limiting credibility gains from demonstrators.

characterized_levers.name: Policy Advocacy Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Policy advocacy shapes procurement. Immediate: Policy proposals submitted → Systemic: 20% greater likelihood of influencing AltID requirements → Strategic: Increased adoption of platform-neutral standards.
options: Focus advocacy on continuity of service and supplier concentration risks, avoiding direct privacy arguments.
Balance continuity arguments with privacy and democratic accountability concerns, broadening the coalition.
Prioritize open-source governance and community-led development models for digital identity, framing platform neutrality as a public good.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Political Risk vs. Coalition Size. Weakness: The options don't consider the potential for regulatory capture by incumbent vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on policy advocacy shaping procurement, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of policy advocacy on influencing AltID requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to advocacy focus.
characterized_levers.description: Policy Advocacy Strategy drives how the project reframes digital identity resilience, procurement neutrality, and supplier concentration into formal proposals and political traction. It coordinates messaging to Digitaliseringsstyrelsen, Folketinget committees, and civil society, translating technical findings into policy language and recommendations. Its objectives include advancing a formal policy proposal, securing a credible fallback path, and increasing the likelihood of platform-neutral requirements in AltID-related designs. Key success metrics include published policy proposals, formal stakeholder engagement, and a measurable uplift in policy attention for platform neutrality.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Key positive interactions with Technical Feasibility Strategy and Coalition Building Strategy. Technical demonstrators provide tangible evidence fueling policy proposals, while coalition allies help socialize policy ideas in Parliament and with Digitaliseringsstyrelsen, increasing momentum and credibility for platform-neutral requirements in AltID procurement and standards discussions.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Potential conflicts with Coalition Building Strategy and Procurement Influence Strategy. If privacy concerns or civil-society friction slow consensus, messaging may fragment the coalition. Conversely, aggressive procurement demands could outpace policy negotiations, creating friction between policy goals and procurement timelines or EU-aligned standards efforts.

characterized_levers.name: Coalition Building Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Coalition strength amplifies advocacy. Immediate: Stakeholder engagement increased → Systemic: 30% stronger advocacy position in procurement discussions → Strategic: Greater political pressure for platform neutrality.
options: Build a narrow coalition focused on security experts and contingency-planning stakeholders.
Expand the coalition to include civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, and academic researchers.
Actively recruit dissenting voices from within the MitID operator and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen to foster internal debate.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Speed vs. Breadth of Support. Weakness: The options fail to address the potential for conflicting priorities within the coalition.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on coalition building to amplify advocacy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of coalition strength on advocacy position, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to coalition composition.
characterized_levers.description: Coalition Building Strategy aims to broaden the base of supporters across security, privacy, civil society, academia, and government stakeholders to increase leverage in procurement and policy. It structures outreach, identifies leadership, mitigates opposition, and sustains momentum across phases. Immediate outcome: more engaged stakeholders; systemic outcome: stronger advocacy position in procurement discussions; strategic outcome: greater political pressure for platform neutrality. Key success metrics include stakeholder engagement counts, cross-constituency endorsements, and public-facing alignment with platform-neutral goals.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Strong synergies with Policy Advocacy Strategy and EU Standards Engagement Strategy. A broader coalition strengthens policy proposals, boosts political legitimacy, and aligns advocacy with EU-standard discussions, enhancing procurement positioning, interoperability messaging, and resilience framing across national and European fora. and accelerating implementation timelines.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Conflicts with Policy Advocacy Strategy and Procurement Influence Strategy. Expanding the coalition can introduce conflicting priorities and slow decision-making, undermining tight procurement timelines. Divergent views among civil-society and privacy groups may complicate messaging that procurement teams can act on or standards bodies endorse.

characterized_levers.name: Procurement Influence Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Procurement influence drives adoption. Immediate: Platform-neutral language included in procurement documents → Systemic: 25% faster scaling through mandated supplier diversity → Strategic: Reduced long-term dependency on Apple and Google.
options: Focus on including general language about supplier concentration risk in AltID procurement documents.
Advocate for specific requirements for platform-neutral access and certified fallback authentication paths.
Propose a 'digital sovereignty bonus' in procurement scoring, rewarding vendors who demonstrably reduce platform dependency.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Specificity vs. Implementability. Weakness: The options don't account for the potential for vendors to game the procurement process.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on procurement influence driving adoption, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of procurement influence on scaling, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to procurement language.
characterized_levers.description: Procurement Influence Strategy focuses on embedding platform-neutral access and certified fallback requirements in AltID-related procurement documents. It translates policy, standards, and feasibility insights into enforceable procurement language and vendor evaluation criteria. Objectives include expanding supplier diversity, accelerating procurement cycles, and reducing long-term platform dependency. Key success metrics: platform-neutral language in procurement docs, faster scaling, and measurable reductions in dependence on Apple/Google in public procurement. It interacts with Technical Feasibility Strategy (evidence-based requirements) and EU Standards Engagement Strategy (alignment with European Wallet frameworks).
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Strong synergy with Technical Feasibility Strategy and EU Standards Engagement Strategy. Demonstrable feasibility informs specific procurement requirements, while EU standards provide a shared basis for language across national and EU procurements, enabling scalable supplier diversity and certified fallback provisions across borders.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Conflicts with Policy Advocacy Strategy and Coalition Building Strategy. Pushing stringent procurement criteria may appear to predefine policy outcomes or alienate coalition partners who favor slower, consensus-driven changes. Additionally, EU standards ambitions could constrain national flexibility or raise compliance costs for vendors.

characterized_levers.name: EU Standards Engagement Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: EU standards engagement creates broader impact. Immediate: Input provided to relevant EU bodies → Systemic: 10% increased alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements → Strategic: Enhanced interoperability and reduced lock-in across Europe.
options: Monitor relevant EU bodies and technical working groups, providing occasional input on interoperability.
Actively engage with EU bodies, advocating for platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms in eIDAS2 and related standards.
Champion a 'sovereign identity sandbox' within the EU Digital Identity Wallet framework to test and validate platform-neutral authentication models.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Resource Allocation vs. Scope of Influence. Weakness: The options don't address the potential for EU standards to be influenced by large platform vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on EU standards engagement creating broader impact, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of EU standards engagement on alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to EU engagement strategies.
characterized_levers.description: EU Standards Engagement Strategy seeks to influence European Digital Identity Wallet materials, eIDAS2 alignment, interoperability, portability, and resilience requirements. It aims to provide input to EU bodies and technical groups, translate national experience into European standards, and reduce cross-border lock-in. Objectives include aligning Danish platform-neutrality goals with EU frameworks, ensuring inclusion of fallback authentication concepts, and strengthening Denmark's position in EU procurement conversations. Key success metrics: documented EU input, alignment with Wallet requirements, and adoption signals in EU design documents.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Strong synergy with Procurement Influence Strategy and Coalition Building Strategy. EU engagement informs procurement language at scale and builds cross-border legitimacy, while a broader coalition ensures Danish positions gain traction in European discussions and align national efforts with EU wallet standards.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Conflicts with Policy Advocacy Strategy and Technical Feasibility Strategy. EU-level alignment can constrain national procurement autonomy or slow the validation of fallback concepts if EU consensus diverges from Denmark-specific needs or technical feasibility limits, creating friction between policy advocacy and practical demonstration timelines.
